title: Public entry points — a tenant-provisioning form, a duplicate CTA block, four bare Telegram links
why: Two of these three rows are true duplication and one is not. `S-169` repeats the hero's two CTAs verbatim — the demo link at L397 is the same URL as L245 — and `S-194` is four bare `https://t.me/malesthetic_bot` links (L681 mobile nav, L834 hero, L2685 footer, L5267 exit-intent) that already are a chat entry, just into a foreign runtime. `S-159` is a different animal: the self-serve tenant-creation path in `maya-start.html`, the same capability as the G07 admin wizard at a lower authority, carrying auto-slug transliteration, the schedule-source branch, the solo_specialist preset, 14-day trial creation and the only two error paths. Under chat-first all three resolve to "start a conversation with Maya" carrying their origin as a parameter — but they are not three CTA implementations grown in three page sections: they live in three different files, and one of them provisions a business.
disappear: After parity, two things: the duplicated final CTA block, so the demo entry contract lives in one place instead of two occurrences that can drift apart, and the four undifferentiated bare Telegram links, which collapse into a single context-carrying entry. The trial form's fate is not settled by its own row — the rationale keeps it "as the fallback for exactness and for anyone who prefers typing fields" while the retirement condition reads RETIRE AFTER PARITY (K16), and that contradiction sits on the one thing the signature is about. All three rows carry that same condition, and the merge target itself is still "to be named" and marked REQUIRES SIGNATURE, so nothing in this group retires on this signature alone.
remain: Every entry point as an entry point, and all of S-159's provisioning behaviour: auto-slug transliteration (L106-110), the internal MAYA calendar vs external CRM choice (L72-73), the solo_specialist preset (L147), branch name and Europe/Moscow timezone (L148-149), 14-day trial creation, and 409 slug-taken / 429 cooldown handling (L164-170). Bare `t.me/malesthetic_bot` links already printed and shared must keep resolving, and the `?start=` payload namespace — `app_<nonce>` (L5742), `linkphone` (L5577), `gift_cert` (L2077) — must not be reordered or collided with: it carries sign-in and loyalty binding, not just marketing attribution. The on-site cabinet is not one of these three rows and is not retired by this signature; S-194 states the constraint that goes with it — for a visitor without Telegram the bot entry is no substitute for the cabinet, and merging the cabinet into the bot would lock those users out entirely. The footer compliance line «Платформа для салонов и барбершопов · Сделано в России · 152-ФЗ» (L404-409) must survive the merge — it is displayed text, not a consent record.
risk: MEDIUM — S-159 is not a conversion experiment: it provisions a tenant, the same write G07 calls the highest-consequence one in the product and rates MEDIUM, reached self-serve rather than through an operator. A conversation that forgets the schedule-source question creates a tenant with no schedule source — a salon that cannot book — the form's password field must not be captured into a transcript, and the row carries the same localhost:3000 API-default hazard as the admin wizard (L101). On S-194, colliding with or reordering the `?start=` payload namespace breaks sign-in and loyalty binding, not just attribution. Not HIGH: no statutory record and no cross-tenant read sits behind this group. S-169 is the only row where conversion testing is genuinely the owner's call, and even there the footer compliance line must survive the merge.
user_impact: Two different people notice, and a third notices almost nothing. A prospective salon owner signing up today fills the seven-input trial form on `сайт и приложение/maya-start.html` (L69-81): brand name, auto-transliterated slug (L111-114), the schedule-source radio (internal MAYA calendar vs external CRM, L72-73), e-mail, owner name, and optional phone and password. Branch name and the Europe/Moscow timezone are NOT inputs — they are derived and hardcoded at L148-149 and the owner is never asked; the proposed enumeration wrongly presents them as questions the conversation must take over, while omitting three fields it actually must (e-mail, owner name, phone). The flow does not end at "tenant created": the done screen renders a one-time `temporary_password` (L190) and auto-hands an owner session into maya-admin (L207-228), so the successor inherits a credential hand-off, not just a questionnaire. Note that the group carries an unresolved contradiction the owner is being asked to sign: S-159's own rationale keeps the typed form "as the fallback for exactness and for anyone who prefers typing fields", while G08's WHAT DISAPPEARS retires "the standalone trial form" — one of the two has to give. A barbershop client on `index.html` today taps any of four identical bare `t.me/malesthetic_bot` links (mobile nav L681, hero L834, footer L2665, exit-intent L5267) and lands in the bot with a generic handoff reply that knows nothing about where they came from; after the merge they meet one door instead of four. The "carries its origin" half is not delivered by this group — nothing in it builds a payload consumer, and an origin-carrying payload scheme already exists in the deployed bot (`ref_<code>`, bot.py L648). A visitor to `maya-site.html` notices nothing in the CTAs: S-169 is a verbatim repeat of the hero block — the demo URL at L397 is byte-identical to L245 — so collapsing it removes a duplicate, not a capability. But the row is "Final CTA + footer", and the footer at L404-409 carries the non-duplicate compliance line «Платформа для салонов и барбершопов · Сделано в России · 152-ФЗ»; "notices nothing at all" holds only if that line survives the merge.
security_impact: No client-side authority check is removed: all three rows are pre-login entry points reachable without auth (roleMode any/any/client, primaryNav false), and tenant creation on S-159 is a server decision — so on the "removed check" axis this group is NEUTRAL. But S-159 is not otherwise security-quiet, and the proposed text spends its paragraph on the wrong hazards. Correcting the direction: the 409 slug-taken and 429 auth_rate_limited handling (L160-168) are NOT "the only uniqueness and anti-abuse guards" — both statuses are issued by the server on POST /onboarding/trial; the page only rewrites the 409 into Russian and runs a local countdown seeded from the server's own Retry-After. A conversational path that drops them loses error legibility, not abuse control (the same is true of the client-side slug regex at L138); claiming it "weakens abuse control on tenant provisioning" manufactures a security loss and contradicts this paragraph's own "already a server decision" clause. The real S-159 obligations are two. First, transcript containment is broader than the password: the password is optional (L81, "пусто — сгенерируем"), so the clean answer is for the conversation never to ask for one — but the completion step renders a one-time `temporary_password` (L190) and writes an owner `access_token` + `refresh_token` bundle into localStorage under a nonce key for hand-off to maya-admin (L207-228), and none of that may become chat content. Second, and unmentioned: L101 takes the API base from a `?api=` URL parameter (falling back to localStorage, then `http://localhost:3000/api`) on an unauthenticated public page that then POSTs owner e-mail, name, phone and password to it — a crafted signup link redirects the entire payload to an arbitrary host and seeds the hand-off with whatever token bundle that host returns. This is pre-existing and the merge neither creates nor closes it, but the successor must not inherit a query-settable API base while also carrying credentials. On S-194, a payload scheme IS an improvement over four bare links — the evidence says so directly — and simultaneously a collision risk; the proposed text's "not an attribution or audit improvement" overcorrects into the opposite error. The collision surface is also larger and more valuable than the three cited rows: the deployed bot consumes `app_<nonce>` sign-in (bot.py L561), `linkphone` phone binding (L526), `redeem_<code>` certificate redemption (L638), `loy_<code>` loyalty-point redemption (L643), `ref_<code>` referral — which already writes state and grants both parties a discount (L648) — and exact-match `gift_cert` (L685). Two of those are staff redemption paths and one is already a marketing-attribution write, so a new origin payload must be prefix-disjoint from all six, and `app_` in particular is prefix-matched (L561) so a colliding payload surfaces to the user as a bogus "sign-in link expired". Note that the identity-consent working copy of bot.py consumes only `app_` and leaves `linkphone`/`gift_cert` inert; the two trees disagree and the payload contract must be specified against the deployed one. Printed and shared bare links must keep resolving. Neither claim touches a frozen limitation: fail-closed counts, STEP_UP reachability, Gate 10 enforcement, approval role-gating and GAP-ATTENDANCE-CONFIRM all live in the post-login widget contract, and none of these three surfaces reaches it.
